criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Every frame is a graded PBR render with one hero, the white van, its kraft load and the ember load bar. Type sits in quiet the art left for it, with no plates. The round 2 world repair is real but narrow. Frame 1 now has the warehouse in haze on the horizon, and so does frame 9 on its left. Frames 7 and 4 are still the only frames that read as a place at an hour. Most of what all three round 1 judges named is still in the pixels. Frame 4's flat yellow polygon is still on the right shoulder (display x 1400 to 1600, y 1560 to 1780). Frame 8's sawtooth shadow still runs down the left carton column (display x 460 to 580, y 860 to 1480), and no tandem shows under the floor, so the van seems to stand on its light boxes and ICC bar. Frame 9's van flank is still cool blue-grey against the warm white everywhere else, and the person is a front-facing mannequin. Frame 3 makes the low-poly tractor the zoom subject: a clay-smooth hood with no seams or road film, a flat black windscreen and blob mirror pods. Frame 5 is still a toy cutaway. Its carton tiles are identical, its floor tapes are pale blocks hanging below the sill over the tyres, and a flat dark strip runs under display y 1780. Frame 6 is a roofless van on a tiled slab whose horizon is a featureless dark band. The Blackland clay the brief describes doesn't read at feed size and there is no warehouse. Too many frames lean on a default or an artifact for the 7 descriptor, though no longer every hub frame.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: Clearly one deck. One hero in one material, a slate sky over a warm brown ground and one grade throughout. The motif changes state in a way a reader could describe: loaded and open (1), running (2 to 4, 7), in section with the tapes (5), counted from above (6), the load face (8), a person beside it (9). machine_qa band ratios run 0.83 to 1.52 with no strobe, and frame 7 is the declared dark cut. Two frames sit outside rather than one. Frame 2 is a flat orthographic side elevation over a painterly grass band, which looks like a different illustrator. Frame 9's van is a cool blue-grey material, unlike the warm white on 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces. 219 is c3/c23 and 45 is c3. 84, 86, 91 and 93 are c27/c7, and 100 is c9. 7 is arm_open. 89 is days_to_year_end, which I checked: 28+30+31 from October 3rd. 3.5 and 2019 are c12/c11. All sources are primary and fetched, three Kodiak pages listed in first_comment.txt. The round 1 looseness is mostly gone. The 93 is now dated 'at the end of August' on the cover, frame 6 and caption line 1. Frame 7 now scopes the disclaimer to 'closing that case by year end', matching c18. The caption says 'mostly Interstate 45'. Three leans remain. (1) Frame 3's dek hangs c6's 'including on surface streets', which belongs to the observer never touching the wheel, onto c5's 'without human intervention'. (2) Frame 4's dek promises 'One post along the road ahead for each day left', but the posts merge into the vanishing point and a reader can't check the count. (3) The close asks 'How many here?' while the run holds c22, Kodiak's own figure of more than 750,000 autonomous miles carrying IKEA goods with an observer aboard, and frame 2 cites that very post (c20, c23, c24). Frame 9 correctly scopes its absence to 'Its release'. The caption's question is not scoped. None of this changes what a reader believes about a fact, so it sits between 7 and 8.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what is happening and when. Kodiak plans to pull the driver on I-45 Dallas to Houston by year end (frames 1, 2, 4). The shipper is IKEA, on its Baytown to Frisco leg (frame 2). The gate is a safety case the company grades itself, at 93 at the end of August (frames 5 to 7). Frame 7 makes the sharpest stake plain: every readiness figure is Kodiak's own. With the TxDMV material removed, though, no public body appears anywhere in nine frames or the caption, and no county is named. The reader is left with nothing to do or watch for. The close is a question the reader has no route to answer. Against the 10 descriptor ('the county, the body, the decision and the deadline are named' and 'what they can do next'), the body is a company, the county is absent and the next step is absent. That is below the 7, where only one stake is stated generally.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: Frame 2 pays at once with the lane, the length, the shipper and 'no one in the cab'. The turn on frame 7 is declared and changes how far to trust the figures. Frame 9's 'More than 3.5 million miles. How many here?' is a pointed close that lands better than a summary would. The cover is the weak link in the feed. 'Not closed yet.' doesn't say driverless or Kodiak, so the reader needs the 5-line dek to know what isn't closed. The 93 is told three times (1, 5, 6), and either 5 or 6 could go without loss. Frame 8's CEO line, 'identified and scheduled', is the company's reassurance placed just before the close, and it slackens the run from 7 to 9.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Plain, unhyped and fair to the company. 'It isn't a safety rating.' and 'Every readiness figure is Kodiak's own.' are good lines. I found no colons, semicolons, dashes, banned words, year-bearing dates or 'And'/'But' openers. Round 1's art-narrating caption line is gone. Flat spots: frame 8's 'final engineering verification and validation' and frame 7's 'forward looking statements' carry filing jargon into the copy. 'The work left.' is a label rather than a line. The caption's 'on 219 miles, mostly Interstate 45, from Dallas to Houston' fences a qualifier with a pair of commas, the construction the house comma rule names. The Blackland and post oak ground in the storyboard still reaches no string, so the Texas texture is city names only.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The ARM series, the van-as-gauge device and the slate, kraft and ember palette are new, and the round 2 repair removed the repeated TxDMV close. The opening is still last week's. Carousel no. 34 (runs/carousel/2026-09-26/copy.json, seven days ago) has the cover kicker 'Interstate 45, Dallas to Houston', identical to this deck's frame 1 kicker. Its frame 2 headline is '219 miles, Kodiak says', against this deck's '219 miles, mostly Interstate 45.' Its frame 3 dek reads 'Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel', on 'deliveries from Lancaster to Houston'. This deck's frame 3 headline is 'Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel.' under the kicker 'Lancaster to Houston'. No. 34's cover dek already said Kodiak plans unsupervised service on the lane by the end of 2026, which this deck's frame 4 restates. The hero is again a sensor-equipped Class 8 tractor on I-45 on four frames (2, 3, 4, 7). stormFront was no. 36's world, and floor tapes with leaders echo no. 40. The cover opens on a negation.

notes_for_panel: No hard fail from this lens. machine_qa.json shows 0 fails, with 9 sky-in-frame warns that the report itself calls a verdict and not a defect. Every slide and caption numeral traces to claims.json or figures.json, and I found no house-rule break in the slide strings or the caption. ship:false is a threshold dissent: 6.49 against round 2's 7.7 rung. LEAD FOR THE OTHER JUDGES ON THE 30 DAY WINDOW, weighed and not failed here. The repair removed no. 34's close, but frames 1 to 3 still reprise no. 34's frames 1 to 3: the identical cover kicker, the same 219 lead on frame 2, and no. 34's frame 3 sentence 'Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel' as this deck's frame 3 headline. The caption's paragraph 3 repeats the observer and year-end beats. I judged this NOT a topic repeat because the decision differs. No. 34 was the state's authorization terms on tx-2026-0188. This deck is the company's self-graded safety case gating its launch, on tx-2026-0198 with the September 8th series, the CEO quote (c39) and the 3.5M miles (c12), none of which no. 34 carried. I charged the overlap to variety instead. A judge who reads the window rule as covering repeated beats, as round 1 did for the close, would apply the same reasoning to frames 2 and 3. Also note that the round 1 art defects all three judges named on frames 4 (yellow polygon), 8 (sawtooth shadow, missing tandem) and 9 (cold van material) were not repaired this round.
one_sentence_fix: Replace frame 3, which reprints no. 34's 'Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel' over the deck's most primitive model, with the IKEA record no. 34 never carried (c21's 1,300 loads and c22's 750,000 observed autonomous miles, set beside frame 9's question without placing them on the lane). In the same pass, delete frame 4's yellow shoulder polygon and clear frame 8's sawtooth carton shadow, the two artifacts all three round 1 judges named that are still in the pixels.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The close crop makes the low-poly tractor the zoom subject. It has a clay-smooth hood with no panel seams or road film, a flat unlit black windscreen, blob mirror pods and a flat grille plate. This is the deck's most primitive frame and it carries the slot's whole detail budget.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Replace the frame (see the fix line), or pull the chase camera back to a medium three-quarter at 6 to 8 m with the lane and a fencerow behind, so the roof sensor bar is the focal and the hood is not. Give the glass an environment-reflective material and put TXT.weather grime on the lower door and steps.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A sawtooth shadow-map artifact still runs down the left carton column (display x 460 to 580, y 860 to 1480). No tandem shows under the floor, so the van reads as standing on its light boxes and ICC bar.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Raise shadow bias and normalBias, or the VSM resolution, on the carton_stack geometry. Lift the camera and pull it back about 2 m so the rear tandem and its contact shadow sit under the floor line.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A flat yellow polygon still lies on the right shoulder (display x 1400 to 1600, y 1560 to 1780), in the deck's best world frame. The delineator posts also merge into the vanishing point, so the 'one post per day' count can't be read.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Delete the stray ground mesh. Shorten the post spacing so the 89th post visibly stands before the horizon with open shoulder beyond it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The roofless van sits on an endless tiled slab whose horizon is a featureless dark band with murk above it. Unlike frames 1 and 9 it got no warehouse, so the counting frame reads as a product shot in a void.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the crane pitch until the warehouse used on frames 1 and 9 sits across the horizon on the upper third behind the hook. Add oil stains and tyre scuffs to the court around the rig.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: It reads as a toy cutaway. The carton tiles are identical along the whole length, the floor tapes are pale blocks hanging below the sill over the tyres, the ember bar floats at ground level, and a flat dark strip runs across the bottom under display y 1780.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lay the three tapes flat on the oak floor inside the section and end the leaders at the sill. Seed lean and flute variation per stack. Extend the court through the bottom strip, or crop it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The van flank turns cool blue-grey against the warm white of every other frame. The kit person stands facing the lens like a mannequin, clear of the van.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Use frame 1's van material and white balance on frame 9. Turn the figure three-quarter toward the open doors at the bumper so she reads the load rather than poses.
